item.title: MBN’s wins Gold, Silver and “Listener’s Choice” at the Signal Awards
item.description: MBN’s podcast “Mirrors,” dedicated to mental health, won gold and the listeners’ choice award at the third annual Signal Awards, it was announced. An episode focused on women’s empowerment and resilience was honored as the most inspirational podcast.

item.title: USAGM CEO condemns Russia’s conviction of RFE/RL journalist Nika Novak
item.description: On November 26, 2024, a Russian court in the Siberian city of Chita sentenced Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL) journalist Nika Novak to four years in prison.

item.title: USAGM networks reached record global audience in FY 2024, according to new report
item.description: The U.S. Agency for Global Media’s networks reached a record 427 million weekly measured global audience in Fiscal Year 2024, as documented in the Agency Performance Report released today. The agency’s audience nearly doubled in the last decade, according to nationally representative surveys measuring the reach and impact of the five journalistic entities USAGM oversees: Voice of America (VOA), Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL), the Office of Cuba Broadcasting (Radio and Television Martí)

item.title: Trump Administration secures release of Radio Liberty journalist Andrey Kuznechyk from detention in Belarus
item.description: After more than three years of imprisonment in Belarus, Radio Liberty journalist Andrey Kuznechyk has been freed.

item.title: Marc Thiessen and Ilan Berman join RFE/RL Board of Directors
item.description: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL) is pleased to welcome two new distinguished members, Marc Thiessen and Ilan Berman, to its Board of Directors.

item.title: USAGM, Senior Advisor Kari Lake cancels obscenely expensive 15-year-lease that burdened the taxpayers and enforces Trump’s Executive Order to drastically downsize agency
item.description: Today, in compliance with President Trump’s Executive Order titled, Continuing the Reduction of the Federal Bureaucracy, dated March 14, 2025, the US Agency for Global Media initiated measures to eliminate the non-statutory components and functions to the maximum extent consistent with applicable law. USAGM and the outlets it oversees will be reduced to their statutory functions and associated personnel will be reduced to the minimum presence and function required by law.

item.title: Lapse in funding
item.description: Due to a lapse in appropriations, USAGM offices are closed. Employees should refer to guidance on usagm.gov/shutdown_guidance for more information.

item.title: U.S. Agency for Global Media Clamps Down on Grantee Rogue Behavior
item.description: The U.S. Agency for Global Media (USAGM) is setting the record straight after a wave of misleading press reports and troubling financial claims pushed out by its own federal grantee, Radio Free Asia (RFA). The grantee, funded entirely by hardworking American taxpayers, has launched into a series of reckless moves, auctioning off broadcast and technology equipment, cutting staff, and suddenly abandoning property. item.description: U.S. Agency for Global Media announces new National Security policy.
